summary: Tier 2, phase C: cut a per-app config seam so a config block no longer has to live in the shared infra/config.AppConfigModel just because mymatasan needs it. Six blocks that were mymatasan-only (camera, decoder, stream, vision, health, recording) — and the model types under them (StreamConfigModel, WebRTCConfigModel, MJPEGFallbackConfigModel, HealthConfigModel, RecordingConfigModel, VisionConfigModel, VisionTrainingConfigModel, VisionDetectorConfigModel) — moved to a new apps/mymatasan/config package. infra/apphost gained an optional AppConfigDecoder interface (DecodeAppConfig(raw, dataDir)) that an app implements to decode its own blocks straight out of the same raw config.json document the shared loader already parsed (AppConfigModel.Raw()); infra/apphost/run.go calls it once, after the shared config is loaded and normalized and before any route is registered, and aborts startup on a decode error. mymatasan also now normalizes its own data-relative paths (the recordings/snapshots root, the YOLO training dir) via Config.Normalize(dataDir) instead of infra/apphost/run.go doing it for it, so the generic application host no longer has hardcoded knowledge of a vision feature. What stayed in the shared model is deliberately narrower: security (encryption-at-rest, also used by myseliasan), pairing/nodeStream (the fleet), notification, and loginSecurity, plus every infra block. Along the way, fixed a real latent bug: infra/config.LoadAppConfiguration used to call json.Decode and discard the returned error, so a single JSON syntax error in config.json silently produced an all-zero config — the app booted on defaults, ignored everything the operator had configured, and said nothing about it. It now returns the error, and both the shared loader and the new apps/mymatasan/config.Load fail loudly on a malformed document. In apps/mymatasan/app, module gained a cfg *mmconfig.Config field populated by DecodeAppConfig, 7 of the 11 config_map.go mappers were retyped from *config.AppConfigModel to *mmconfig.Config, and the wiring struct gained an appCfg field plus a new validate() method that fails startup naming any wiring field left unset — added because appCfg was in fact left unset on the first cut of this change and panicked in registerRoutes at boot, a bug class that was worth guarding against for every field, not just this one.
compatibility: No config.json format change: the moved blocks stay at the top level of config.json exactly where they already are (NOT nested under an "app" key), so no deployed config file needs to change or be migrated. Every existing mymatasan install continues to read camera/decoder/stream/vision/health/recording settings from the same JSON paths as before. Behavior is unchanged for a correctly-configured install; the LoadAppConfiguration error-propagation fix only changes behavior for an install that already had a malformed config.json (which was silently running on all-zero defaults) - such an install will now fail to start with a clear parse error instead of booting silently misconfigured, which is the intended, safer behavior. myseliasan and myidsan are unaffected: they never read the six moved blocks, and the shared AppConfigModel they use is unchanged in shape for the fields they do read. This unblocks MyIotSan (docs/MYIOTSAN_PLAN.md), which needed a config model that isn't pre-loaded with mymatasan's camera/vision domain.
